chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muammar ibn Khallaad who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Sometimes I see a dream, so I interpret it, and the dream is upon what you interpret.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hassan (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of dream interpretation in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the authority of the Imams in dream interpretation (ta'bir), suggesting that their insight aligns the subjective vision with objective spiritual reality. In Shia scholarship, this is often viewed as a manifestation of their infallible knowledge (‘ismah) or inspired understanding, distinguishing their interpretations from those of ordinary scholars. It establishes a theological basis for relying on the Ahl al-Bayt for resolving ambiguities in spiritual experiences.

en.hubeali: H 14975 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muammar Bin Khallaad who said:
I heard Abu Al-Hassanasws saying: ‘Sometimes Iasws see the dream, so Iasws interpret it, and the dream is upon what you interpret’.
en.sarwar: 528. b – From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzaal, from AL-Hassan Bin Jahm who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassan (a.s.) saying: ‘The dream is upon what interpretation you give it’. So I said to him (a.s.) that, ‘Some of our companions are reporting that the dream of the king was a confused dream’. So Abu Al-Hassan (a.s.) said: ‘A woman saw a dream during the era of the Rasool Allah (saww) that a pillar of her house had broken. So she came to the Rasool Allah (saww) and related the dream to him (saww). The Prophet (saww) said to her: ‘Your husband will come to you safely’; and her husband had gone away (in a caravan). So he came just as the Prophet (saww) said that he would. Then he went away from her for another time. She saw in the dream as if a pillar of her house had broken. So she came to the Prophet (saww) and related the dream to him (saww). So he (saww) said to her: ‘Your husband will come to you safely’. So he came as he (saww) had said he would. Then her husband went away for a third time. She saw in her dream that a pillar of her house had broken. She met a left-handed man (a fortune teller), so she related her dream to him. The man said to her, ‘The evil. Your husband is dead’. (As the news of her dead husband) reached the Prophet (saww), so he (saww) said: ‘If only he had interpreted it for her in a good way’.
